results.line: How Redbelly's nodes agree on the next block, with no leader.
One block wins. The rest is wasted.
Every node plays a similar role.

results.line: It makes sure everyone on the network is who they say they are.
Access needs a credential from an accredited issuer.
Apps state who qualifies, such as accredited investors.
Built on the W3C verifiable credential data model.
A digital proof about you, signed by whoever checked it.
You keep it and share proof when asked.
You. It stays in your wallet.
Reusable. Your data is not copied to every app.
Prove something is true without revealing the data behind it.
An app asks a yes or no question.
Your wallet proves it. No data shown.
Shows only the fields asked for.
Shows no data. Only the proof.
Funds and companies use it to issue and manage tokenised assets.
Identity and wallet. Credentials gate every holder.
Every holder verified. Every transfer checked against the rules.
On Redbelly, an asset can carry its own rules.
Every transfer is checked against them first.
Rules follow it into other apps.
Nodes that try to cause disagreement leave proof.
Transactions can be tied to a responsible party.
Only if 1 in 3 or more nodes are faulty.
Their signed messages can name them.
Excluded from consensus with enough proof.

notes: printed on the artwork (source: Proof comes from faulty nodes trying to cause disagreement among honest nodes: they leave signed traces that honest nodes combine into undeniable proofs of fraud.)
printed on the artwork (source: The trigger is honest nodes disagreeing on the next block. The system can then, eventually, name the faulty nodes responsible (at least a third of the nodes, n/3).)
printed on the artwork (source: Disagreement is only possible with 1 in 3 or more faulty nodes: below that, DBFT is proven safe.)
printed on the artwork (source: Once honest nodes have enough proofs of fraud, a membership change removes the faulty nodes from the consensus committee.)
